title: Compatibility Gateway: map legacy Chat Completions v1 to Redwood streaming + tool-call protocol with high fidelity
creator: Aisha Ramanathan
description:
Implement a compatibility gateway that accepts legacy Chat Completions v1-style HTTP requests and emits responses that match the OpenAI-compatible streaming and function/tool-call semantics expected by existing customers. The gateway will translate inbound request shapes (messages[], max_tokens, stop, function_call hints, etc.) into Redwood's internal streaming protocol, and translate back streaming fragments, function_call events, structured outputs, and final deltas into the canonical Chat Completions response frames. The goal is parity with common OpenAI client behavior (including partial deltas, tool call start/finish, and deterministic structured output shapes) while preserving Redwood runtime guarantees (latency SLOs, backpressure, KV cache reuse).

Scope: HTTP/1.1 POST -> /v1/chat/completions compatibility endpoint; streaming via chunked SSE-like frames; mapping of function_call/name/arguments to Redwood tool metadata; graceful fallback when target model doesn't support tool calls (return 415-style error or emulate by returning suggested tool invocation). Must include comprehensive test harness and canary rollout plan.

Non-goal: native rewrites of prompt logic, or changing customer payload schemas beyond translation layer. We will not expose internal runtime primitives on the compatibility surface.
technical_notes: Implementation language: Go (service in inference-gateway repo) to reuse existing HTTP streaming utilities.
Internal transport: gRPC streaming between gateway and model workers; gateway will materialize an intermediate canonical message envelope to decouple transforms from runtime changes.

Canonical envelope fields: request_id, messages[], functions[], max_tokens, stop_tokens, preferred_streaming_mode. This envelope is represented as typed protobuf on the internal path; gateway keeps a lightweight JSON<>proto mapping cache for hot client schemas.

Streaming mapping: inbound chunked SSE from model worker contains event types 'delta', 'tool_call_start', 'tool_call_chunk', 'tool_call_end', 'metadata'. The gateway must reframe these into OpenAI-compatible streaming lines (data: { ... }) with 'choices[0].delta' and 'choices[0].finish_reason' semantics.

Function/tool mapping: Redwood tool metadata -> OpenAI function schema mapping table. When model emits a tool_call object we translate fields to { name, arguments } and stream 'role: assistant' deltas that include function_call in the final object per OpenAI clients expectations.

Idempotency and ordering: use request_id + monotonic chunk index. Gateway will detect duplicate chunks and drop silently. For reconnects, gateway supports resume via last-seen chunk index header if client supplies a compatible resume token.

Performance trade-offs: translation adds ~0.6ms median per-request CPU overhead in microbenchmarks. Mitigation: fast-path for requests with no functions and no structured output enforcement; bench with dedicated autoscale policy for compatibility gateway service.

Telemetry: emit metrics 'compat.gateway.requests', 'compat.gateway.stream_chunks', 'compat.gateway.tool_calls', 'compat.gateway.failures' with tags model=, region=, tenant=. Traces should include transform_time and stream_rewrite_time spans.
Security: request body may include PII. Ensure the gateway honors customer-managed encryption and does not log full messages. KMS-review ticket required (see links).
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/chat/completions accepts legacy payloads and returns identical non-streamed payloads for simple cases (parity test).
Streaming clients receive a sequence of SSE-like 'data:' frames that reconstruct into equivalent OpenAI streaming events including partial content deltas and final finish reason.
Function/tool-call sequences are emitted as start/chunk/end events, reconstructed by compatible clients into a single function_call object with aggregated arguments.
Automated e2e test harness verifies 99% chunk ordering and no data loss under simulated packet loss and reconnect scenarios.
Compatibility gateway goes through canary rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with no more than 5% increase in p95 latency for affected customers during each step.
Security review completed and artifacts linked; no plaintext customer data written to logs by default.
Docs added to developer portal showing mapping examples for: simple chat, streaming with function_call, structured output and tool-call fallback behaviors.
